entries.effect: 0, and 0 IS NOT A MEMBER of tls_protocol_version_t: the enum is TLSv10 0x0301, TLSv12 0x0303, TLSv13 0x0304, DTLSv12 0xfefd, every one a REAL version (SecProtocolTypes.h:58-66). The header promises only "A tls_protocol_version_t value" and names no absence, so this is a sentinel the port manufactures, and the cost is stated: A CALLER CANNOT TELL IT FROM A VALUE THE ENUM DOES NOT DEFINE. It never reports a negotiated version, because nothing on 6.1.3 negotiates one
entries.reason: the header declares a TYPE and a function and the port supplies the object under its own name: as clang -E emits it, sec_protocol_metadata_t is `NSObject<OS_sec_protocol_metadata> * __attribute__((objc_independent_class))`. The class is DELIBERATELY EMPTY - this header has no setter and nothing in 6.1.3 ever produces a metadata, one being handed to a TLS callback by the handshake that negotiated it - so a held value would be a number that LOOKS negotiated with no caller able to have set it
